items.title: Amgen vs. Regeneron: Higher Dividends Now or Bigger Growth Later?
items.summary: One biotech pays retirees a bigger check today, while the other carries no net debt and is growing far faster. We put Amgen and Regeneron side by side on income, valuation, and growth to see which one earns a spot in a retirement account.

items.title: 3 Biotech Stocks That Actually Pay Dividends and Keep Raising Them
items.summary: Biotech usually torches cash and dilutes shareholders to fund the next trial. Three drugmakers flip that script, and the one with the smallest yield may be hiding the sturdiest payout of all. Coverage, not yield, tells the real story.

items.title: Amgen’s Repatha shows cost-effectiveness in cardiovascular study
items.summary: Amgen (AMGN) announced new data at the American Heart Association Scientific Sessions 2026 that further strengthen the case for more intensive lowering of low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, or LDL-C, with Repatha – evolocumab – in high-risk patients. The findings add to evidence supporting Repatha for people with and without a prior cardiovascular event. New late-breaking findings show that Repatha was a highly cost-effective treatment option for high-risk patients without a prior heart attack

items.title: What Does Amgen (AMGN) Mean For Heart Attack Risk After New Repatha Data?
items.summary: Amgen (NasdaqGS:AMGN) reported new real world data showing Repatha cut heart attack risk more than ezetimibe in patients with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. The large scale analysis compared outcomes for high risk patients treated with Repatha versus ezetimibe in routine clinical practice.
